General Questions
Who are you?

Al Anfal Doc is the trading name of Al Anfal Documents Clearing Services LLC, a Dubai team that prepares and submits company, licence, attestation, labour and residency paperwork for business owners, investors and expatriates.
What does your process look like?

We review what you need, confirm the steps, documents and fees in writing, prepare and check your file, submit it to the right authority and follow it until the authority issues its decision. You receive copies of every submission and the final documents.
Do you issue visas, licences or permits?
No. Licences, visas and permits are issued by the UAE authorities. We provide document preparation, processing and application support, and we follow each file until the authority has decided.
No. Every decision is made by the relevant authority. A complete and correct file reduces avoidable rejections, but approval is never ours to promise.
In which languages do you prepare documents?
We prepare documents in Arabic and English, including bilingual contracts, memoranda and powers of attorney, and we arrange certified translation where an authority requires it.
Can a foreigner own 100% of a company in Dubai?

For most mainland activities, yes, since the 2021 reforms. A limited list of strategic activities needs a UAE partner or special approval, and some professional activities have extra conditions. We confirm the rule for your activity before you decide on shares.
What is the difference between mainland and free zone?

A mainland company is licensed by the Department of Economy and Tourism and can trade across the UAE. A free zone company is licensed by a free zone authority, often with a simpler setup, but with limits on trading directly in the mainland market.
What taxes apply to a Dubai company?

Corporate tax applies at 9% on taxable income above AED 375,000, with 0% up to that amount, and every company must register with the Federal Tax Authority. VAT registration applies above the threshold. Your home country may also have rules, so ask a tax adviser.
Do I need an office for a mainland licence?

A mainland licence normally needs a registered tenancy contract (Ejari). Free zones often include a flexi desk or office in the package. See our guide to virtual offices and Ejari for what each licence accepts.
How long does company formation take?
A simple setup can take several days, and a setup that needs external approvals or a new tenancy can take a few weeks. We give a timeline per step after reviewing your activity and premises.
What does visa processing support include?

Document preparation, processing and application support for residence and labour files: checking the documents, typing the applications, submitting them through the authorised channels and following them until the authority decides.
What is the order of steps for a new employee?

The company licence and quota come first, then the labour contract and work permit, then the entry permit or status change, medical fitness, biometrics, visa stamping and the Emirates ID, with health insurance in place.
Do I need to be in the UAE for my residence file?
Some steps, such as medical fitness, biometrics and the Emirates ID, need the applicant in the UAE. Other steps can be prepared remotely through a power of attorney or an online application.
Can you sponsor my family?

A resident can apply to sponsor eligible family members according to the authority's rules. We prepare the documents and support the application, and we confirm current requirements such as income and accommodation before you apply.
What if an application is rejected?
We read the reason, correct the file and resubmit where the rules allow. Typical causes are mismatched names, expired documents or an incomplete sequence.
What does document attestation mean?

It is the chain of steps that proves a signature or seal on a document is genuine so that another country's authorities accept it. For UAE use it commonly involves a notary, an apostille or legalisation in the home country, embassy attestation where required and the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
How long does attestation take?
It depends on the countries involved and the number of steps. Some routes finish within days and others take several weeks. We give an estimate once we know the document and the country.
Do my documents need an Arabic translation?
Usually yes for UAE authorities, courts and many banks. A certified translator normally translates the document after attestation, so the stamps are translated too.
What is a power of attorney and when do I need one?

A power of attorney lets another person sign or act for you. Owners abroad use one so a representative can complete licence, bank and government steps in Dubai. A narrow, clearly worded power with an end date is safest.
How much does a notary charge in Dubai?

Under the Dubai fee schedule amended in 2025, a notary charges AED 300 per signature attested on an instrument or proxy. Drafting, translation and later attestation steps are extra, and we confirm the full amount before you proceed.
Fees, Payments & Timelines
Are government fees included in your fee?
No. Government fees are passed through at the amount the authority charges and are shown separately, so you can see exactly what is official and what is our professional fee.
Can I pay from outside the UAE?
Yes, by bank transfer. Fees are in dirhams, which are pegged to the US dollar at 3.6725, so dollar payments convert at a stable rate and other currencies convert at your bank's rate.
Why do timelines differ between customers?

Timing depends on the authority's review, the number of departments involved and whether the file is complete the first time. We give an estimate at the start and tell you promptly if an authority asks for more.

What does it cost to set up a company?

Can I run the company from my home country?

How do I bring money from my home country to set up and run the business?

Can you also open the bank account?

We prepare the company documents banks ask for and introduce the file, but the bank decides whether to open the account and sets its own requirements and timeline. See our business bank account service for more.
Is company formation a good way to get residency?

A licensed company can sponsor residence visas for its owners and employees according to its licence and office size. Residency is granted by the authorities, and the rules differ by company type. We prepare the files and explain the conditions.

What does government transactions liaison actually include?

It covers the full chain around a government file: checking the requirements, preparing and typing the application, submitting it through the right channel, tracking it, paying the official fees, and collecting the result. The authority still makes the decision; we manage the paperwork and the follow-up.
Is a PRO the same as a lawyer or a consultant?

No. A PRO focuses on procedure: forms, approvals, submissions and renewals. A lawyer gives legal advice and a consultant plans the business structure. We work alongside both, and we will tell you when a question needs legal advice rather than paperwork.
Can I use your team if I live outside the UAE?

Yes. A notarised power of attorney or a company authorisation letter lets us submit and collect on your behalf. Documents signed abroad usually need notarisation and legalisation first, and we explain which steps apply to the country you sign in.
Which Dubai authorities do you deal with most often?

The Department of Economy and Tourism for licences, MOHRE for labour transactions, GDRFA and the ICP for residency, the Dubai Land Department for tenancy registration, Dubai Municipality for activity approvals and the Dubai Courts notary for attestations.
How do you charge for government fees?

Official fees are passed through at the amount the authority charges and are listed separately from our professional fee. You see the breakdown before you approve the work, so there is no mixed 'all-in' number to decode.
How long does a typical filing take?

Straightforward submissions can be completed the same day. Anything that needs an inspection, an external approval or a second department can take days or a few weeks. We give a realistic window at the start and tell you quickly if an authority changes the process.
What happens if a government office rejects the file?

We read the rejection reason, correct the file and resubmit it. Most rejections come from small errors such as an expired document or a mismatched name spelling, and a pre-submission check removes many of them.
Do you remind us about renewals?
Yes. We keep a renewal calendar for trade licences, tenancy contracts, labour and residency documents and insurance, and we contact you well before each date so you can avoid late penalties.
I pay in a different currency. Does that complicate things?

Government fees are charged in UAE dirhams, which are pegged to the US dollar at 3.6725. We invoice in dirhams and can accept bank transfer from abroad; your bank's exchange rate and transfer charges apply on your side.
Will I be able to see what you have submitted for me?
Yes. You get copies of every submission, the transaction numbers and the final documents, and we keep a record per company so a new manager or accountant can pick up where the last one stopped.
Do you issue visas?
No. Visas and permits are issued by the UAE authorities. We provide document preparation, processing and application support, and we follow your file until the authority has decided.

The company licence and quota come first, then the labour contract and work permit, then the entry permit or status change, medical fitness, biometrics, visa stamping and Emirates ID, with insurance in place. We keep this order on one checklist.
What documents are needed?

Typically the company licence and establishment record, the employee's passport and photograph, a contract or offer, and, for some categories, attested educational or civil documents. We give the exact list once we know the category.
How long does a residence file take?
It depends on the category and the authority's review, and queries can add time. We give an estimate at the start and update you at each step.
Can the owner or investor of a company also be processed?

A licensed company can sponsor residence for its owners and partners according to the licence and premises, and some investment categories have separate routes. We confirm the right category for your situation.
Do my educational certificates need attestation?
For some categories, yes. The route depends on the country where the certificate was issued, and we explain it. See our document clearing service.
Is medical fitness mandatory?

For residence it generally is. The medical test, usually done at an approved centre, is part of the file, and the visa and Emirates ID steps depend on it. See our page on Emirates ID and medical fitness.
Can you handle renewals and cancellations?
Yes. We track expiry dates, prepare renewals and process cancellations when staff leave, so the company's quota and records stay accurate.
How are the fees paid when I am abroad?
Authority fees are charged in dirhams. The dirham is pegged to the US dollar at 3.6725, so transfers in dollars convert predictably; other currencies convert at your bank's rate.
What is the difference between legalisation and apostille?

Both prove that a signature or seal on a public document is genuine. An apostille is a single certificate used between countries that joined the Hague Apostille system. Legalisation is the longer chain used where that system does not apply. We confirm which applies for your country.
Do I need embassy attestation for UAE use?
Often yes for documents coming from abroad, followed by attestation by the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The exact route depends on the country and the document, so we confirm it before you begin.
It depends on the countries involved and the number of steps. Some routes finish within days, others take several weeks. We give an estimate once we know the document and the country.
Do documents need to be translated into Arabic?
Usually yes for UAE authorities, courts and many banks. Translation is normally done by a certified translator after the document has been attested, so the stamps are translated too.
Can you clear documents from my home country without me travelling?
Yes. Many steps can be done through courier and local agents, and you may only need to sign before a notary at home. We outline what can be done remotely for your country.
How old can a document be?

Some authorities want recent certificates, for example a good standing certificate issued within the last few months. We check the requirement of the receiving authority before you order the document.
What if the document has a spelling mistake?
Correct it at the source before attesting. A mistake that is found after attestation usually means repeating the chain. We check names against the passport and licence before the first step.
Do you handle documents from Asia, Europe and the Americas?
Yes. The route differs by country, but the logic is the same. We keep a checklist by country and update it when rules change.
How are fees paid, and in what currency?
Each authority charges in its own currency. We invoice in dirhams and list the authority fees separately. The dirham is pegged to the US dollar at 3.6725, so dollar transfers are easy to convert.
Can UAE documents be used abroad?

Yes, through a reverse chain of notary, Ministry of Foreign Affairs attestation and, for the foreign destination, an embassy attestation or an apostille where available. We map the steps for each destination country.
When should I start renewing my trade licence?
Around 30 to 45 days before the expiry date is a common recommendation. That leaves time to renew the tenancy registration, correct any document problems and handle a query from the authority.
What is needed to renew a licence?

The current licence, a valid registered tenancy contract, passport and Emirates ID copies for the owners and manager, any required activity approvals and the signed application. We prepare the list for your exact licence type.
How long does a renewal take?
Reported processing times range from one to seven working days once the file is complete. Delays usually come from an expired tenancy registration, missing approvals or a mismatch in documents.
How much does renewal cost?
Fees depend on licence type and activity, so there is no single figure. We give the official fee in your quote, with our professional fee shown separately.
What happens if my licence expires?

Late renewal can bring penalties and may affect visas, banking and contracts. Published reports about the exact amounts and any grace period differ, so we confirm the current rule before advising you.
Can I add a new activity to my licence?
Yes, subject to the authority's rules. Some activities need an external approval first and some need a change in the premises. We check the activity list and approvals before we file.
Do I need to update my memorandum when I change a partner?
Yes. A new partner, a transfer of shares or a new manager requires an updated memorandum, normally notarised, before the licence is amended. See our page on MOA drafting and amendments.
Can I renew while I am abroad?
Yes, with a power of attorney or a company authorisation letter, or by approving the application online. Where a signature or presence is needed, we tell you in advance.
Does a licence renewal affect my corporate tax obligations?

Renewal itself does not, but the company's corporate tax registration and filing are separate obligations with the Federal Tax Authority. Companies should keep both current, and your accountant can confirm filing dates.
Can you remind us about the next renewal?
Yes. We keep a renewal calendar for your licence, tenancy and related documents and contact you ahead of each deadline, so you are not relying on memory.
What is a certified legal translation?
A translation prepared by an approved translator and stamped as an accurate rendering, accepted by courts and government bodies.
Which languages do you translate?
Arabic and English are the most common pairs, with other languages available on request.
Can you translate and attest in one go?
Yes. We can handle the translation and the follow-on notarisation or attestation as one service.
Can you guarantee my bank account will be approved?
No. Banks make their own compliance decisions. We prepare a complete application and introduce you to banks that fit your profile to improve your chances.
What documents are needed to open a corporate account?
Typically the trade licence, memorandum of association, shareholder and manager IDs, proof of address and a business profile. Requirements vary by bank.
Do I need to be in the UAE to open an account?
Some banks require an in-person visit and others support remote steps. We confirm the process for your chosen bank.
Who is business consulting for?
Founders, investors and established companies that need guidance on structure, compliance or entering the UAE market.
Do you give legal or tax advice?
We provide practical business and regulatory guidance. For formal legal or tax opinions we recommend a licensed adviser and can coordinate with one.
How do I get started?
Book a consultation and tell us your goals. We recommend the best structure and the next steps.
What is the UAE golden visa?
A long-term residence visa for eligible investors, entrepreneurs and skilled professionals. Eligibility depends on the category and current rules.
Can I get residence as a company owner?
Yes, owners and partners of a UAE company can usually apply for residence linked to the company. Requirements depend on the licence type.
Can my family be included?
Eligible residents can generally sponsor family members. We prepare the documentation for each sponsored person.
Does every Dubai business need Dubai Municipality approval?

No. It depends on the licensed activity and the premises. Food related activities and some health, safety or premises-based activities need it, while many consultancy and online services do not. The activity code on the licence is the starting point for the check.
Is a trade licence enough to start trading?

Not always. The licence permits the activity, but a regulated activity may need the municipal approval and sometimes a fire safety approval before opening. Check the approval list for your activity before you invest in fit-out.
What is the food safety plan I keep hearing about?

It is a documented system, commonly based on HACCP, that shows how food is received, stored, prepared and served safely. Food establishment applications normally include it, and it should be kept up to date after approval.
How long does municipal approval take?

Food activities often take a few weeks when the premises, layout and documents are ready. Delays usually come from incomplete plans, equipment that does not match the application or an inspection that has to be repeated.
What does it cost?
Fees depend on the activity and premises and published estimates vary widely. We confirm the official fees after reviewing your case and show them separately from our professional fee.
Can I apply before I have a tenancy contract?

Premises-based approvals usually need a confirmed location, so the lease and its registration normally come first. We can prepare the rest of the file in advance so submission is quick once the address is fixed.
Who handles fire safety approval?

Fire safety is usually reviewed by Civil Defence and building permissions sit with the building owner or the relevant authority, not with the municipality's food team. We include both in the project plan so nothing is forgotten.
I am setting up from abroad. Can you attend the inspection?

Yes. With a power of attorney or authorisation letter, our team can receive the inspector, sign the visit report where permitted and follow up on remarks, and we send you photographs and the written outcome.
Are there tax or accounting points I should plan for at the same time?

Yes. Dubai companies also register for corporate tax with the Federal Tax Authority and, above the threshold, for VAT. Corporate tax applies at 9% on taxable income above AED 375,000, and registration is required even where the rate is 0%. Confirm your own position with a tax adviser.
What if the application is refused or corrections are requested?

We read the remarks, update the plan or documents and resubmit. Most requests are for layout changes, missing certificates or clarifications on the activity, and they are usually solved faster when one person manages the whole file.
Is DED the same as DET?

Yes. The Department of Economic Development was renamed the Department of Economy and Tourism. Many forms, documents and conversations still use the older DED name, but the licensing role is the same.
Do free zone companies use DET?

Generally no. A free zone company is licensed and supervised by its own free zone authority, which has its own forms and fees. A mainland licence from DET is needed to trade directly in the Dubai market without a distributor.
What is the difference between commercial, professional and industrial licences?

Commercial covers trading in goods and some services, professional covers expertise-based services, and industrial covers manufacturing. The type decides the allowed activities, the premises needed and in some cases the ownership rules.
Can a foreigner own 100% of a Dubai mainland company?

For most activities, yes, since the 2021 reforms. A limited list of strategic activities still needs a UAE partner or special approval, and some professional activities have extra conditions. We confirm the current rule for your activity before you decide on the structure.
What is initial approval?

It is the department's first approval of the trade name and activities, given before the tenancy and memorandum are finalised. It tells you the proposed company is acceptable so that you can sign the lease and documents with confidence.
How long does adding an activity take?

When the activity needs no external approval and the file is complete, it can be done quickly, sometimes within a day. Activities that need another authority's approval take as long as that approval does.
What if my Ejari expires before I renew the licence?

The tenancy registration normally has to be valid for the licence to be processed, so renew it first. Our service tracks both dates and alerts you in advance. See our page on Ejari registration for the process.
Do I need to be in Dubai to file?

Not always. With a notarised power of attorney or an authorisation letter, we can submit and collect on your behalf. Some steps, such as signing a memorandum, may need a notary, and we guide you on when.
Are there any tax steps connected to a new licence?

A newly licensed company should register for corporate tax with the Federal Tax Authority, even if its profit will be inside the 0% band up to AED 375,000, and for VAT once it passes the threshold. We coordinate the timing with your accountant.
Can you cancel a licence and close the company file?

Yes. Cancellation needs the labour and residency files, the tenancy and bank matters to be settled in the right order. We prepare the closing checklist and submit the cancellation so that no penalty or hold remains on the owners.
What is the difference between a general and a special POA?

A special POA allows a specific task or transaction, such as renewing a licence. A general POA covers a wider set of matters. For company and property affairs a special POA with a clear scope and end date is usually safer.

Under the Dubai fee schedule published in 2025, a notary charges AED 300 for each signature attested on an instrument or proxy. Extra translation, drafting and later attestation steps are separate. We confirm the full amount in your quote.
Can I sign a POA for the UAE while I am abroad?

Yes. You sign before a notary in the country where you are, then the document is legalised or apostilled according to that country's rules and attested by the UAE embassy and the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs. We confirm the exact steps for your country first.
Does the POA have to be in Arabic?

UAE authorities generally require Arabic or a certified Arabic translation. We draft both versions together so that the English and Arabic text match and the document is accepted without a second round.
How long is a POA valid?
It is valid for the period stated in the document, or until it is revoked. We recommend setting a clear end date and revoking it formally once the task is done.
Can a PRO or manager use my POA at the bank?
Banks apply their own rules and may ask for their own form or extra attestation. We check the bank's requirement in advance so the POA is drafted in the form it will accept.
Can I cancel or change a POA?
Yes. A POA can be revoked through a notarised revocation, and a new one can be issued. Tell the agent and any authority or bank that holds a copy so they stop relying on the old document.
Do you offer online drafting?
Yes. We take the details online, send the draft for your approval and arrange notarisation and attestation afterwards. Some steps still need a signature in person before a notary.
Are there tax or currency issues with a POA for a foreign investor?

A POA itself is not a tax document, but it may be used for steps such as opening a bank account or registering for corporate tax. Fees are paid in dirhams, which are pegged to the US dollar at 3.6725, so your own bank's exchange rate applies on the transfer.
What if the signature on my passport is different from my POA signature?
Differences can lead to rejection. Sign the same way on all documents and tell us if your signature has changed, so we can advise on a declaration or a new identity document before filing.
What is a Memorandum of Association?

It is the founding document of a company. It records the shareholders, capital, activities, management rules and procedures for changes such as share transfers. Banks, authorities and buyers rely on it to see who controls the company.
When do I need to amend the MOA?

Whenever something it records changes: a shareholder joins or leaves, shares move between partners, capital changes, a manager or signatory changes, or the activity list changes. The amendment is then filed so that the licence and the memorandum match.
Do all partners have to sign an amendment?

Usually yes, or they sign through a power of attorney. If one partner sells shares, the others normally have a right of first refusal and must sign or waive it in writing. The notary and the authority expect to see that.
Is notarisation always needed?

For most mainland LLC changes the amended memorandum or addendum is notarised before filing. Free zone companies follow their authority's own procedure, which may differ. We confirm the requirement for your authority.
How long does an amendment take?
We prepare the draft in one to two working days. The notary appointment and the authority's processing add time, and some changes need extra approvals. We give an estimate for your case at the start.
Can partners abroad sign?

Yes. They can sign before a notary in their country and have the document legalised for UAE use, or authorise someone in the UAE through a notarised power of attorney. We advise on the faster route for your country.
Will my bank need the new MOA?
Almost certainly. Banks ask for the updated memorandum and licence when signatories or shareholders change. Updating the bank file at the same time avoids payment delays.
What does a share transfer cost?

There is a notary charge per signature, plus the authority's fee for the amendment, plus our professional fee. The authority's fee depends on the licence type and the change. We list each item in the quote.
Does a change of shareholder affect taxes?

It may. Changes in ownership can affect the company's corporate tax position, and share purchase prices can raise tax questions in a seller's home country. Ask your tax adviser, and we can coordinate the paperwork with them.
Do you advise on legal disputes between partners?
We handle the documents and filings. If there is a dispute or a legal question about the memorandum, we recommend a UAE lawyer and can coordinate with them on the drafting and filing.
What is a typing centre and what does it do?

A typing centre prepares and submits applications for government services on behalf of customers. In practice that means entering your details correctly into the authority's system or form, attaching the right documents and paying the official fee.
Do I need Arabic for every document?

Not for every document, but many UAE authorities require Arabic or an Arabic translation, especially for contracts, memoranda and powers of attorney. We prepare the Arabic version with the English so they match.
Can you draft a contract from my notes?

Yes. We turn the agreed terms into a clear contract or addendum in English and Arabic. For legal advice on the terms, we recommend a UAE lawyer, and we can format the final text after the lawyer approves.
What documents do you need to type an application?
Usually passports, Emirates IDs, the trade licence, the tenancy contract and any earlier application. We tell you the exact list once we know the transaction.
How do you avoid spelling mistakes in names?
We copy names from the passport and the Emirates ID, compare them to the licence, and flag any difference before filing. Many rejections come from differences in spelling or order of names.
How long does legal typing take?
Standard forms are generally prepared the same day. Contracts, bilingual texts and long documents take longer, and we give a time estimate when you send the request.
Is certified translation part of this service?

Typing and drafting are separate from certified translation. If a document needs to be translated by a certified translator, we arrange that through our legal translation service and then type or format the result.
Can I pay in a foreign currency?
We invoice in dirhams. The dirham is pegged to the US dollar at 3.6725, so bank transfers from abroad convert at your bank's rate, and we can share a pro-forma invoice for your records.
Do I need to be in Dubai to use the service?
No. You can send scans of your documents and approve the draft online. Where a signature must be given in person or before a notary, we explain how to do it from your country.
What if an authority changes its form?
We update the format as soon as the authority publishes the change. If a form changes while your application is in progress, we correct and resubmit it.
What is Ejari?

Ejari is the Dubai system that registers tenancy contracts with the Dubai Land Department. The Ejari certificate shows that the lease is registered, and for businesses it serves as proof of the registered address for the licence.
Do I need Ejari for a trade licence?
A mainland trade licence normally requires a registered tenancy for the business premises. Free zones use their own lease documents. Check your licensing authority's current rule before you rent.
Can I use a virtual office for a mainland licence?

Advisers report that plain virtual office contracts often do not meet the mainland requirement because Ejari needs a valid lease. Some flexi desk providers issue Ejari-compliant leases for certain professional activities. We confirm with the authority before you commit.
Can a virtual office or flexi desk work in a free zone?
Often yes. Many free zones accept a flexi desk or similar package as the registered address for the licence. The exact rule depends on the free zone and the licence type.
How much does Ejari registration cost?
Recent guides report about AED 177.75 for online registration, including fees and VAT, and a higher amount at a trustee centre. Fees can change, so we confirm the current figure.
How long does Ejari registration take?
With a signed contract and complete documents, online registration can be fast. Delays usually come from missing landlord documents or utility details.
When do I renew Ejari?
Renew it when the tenancy contract is renewed, and always before you renew the trade licence, because the licence file depends on a valid certificate. Our calendar service tracks both dates.
What documents are needed for registration?

The signed tenancy contract, the landlord's title deed, the tenant's passport and Emirates ID or trade licence, and electricity and water connection details. We prepare the exact list once we see the contract.
Does the office rent depend on my country of origin?

No. Rent depends on the area, size and building, not on nationality. International payments are made in dirhams; the dirham is pegged to the US dollar at 3.6725, so only your own bank's exchange and transfer fees apply.
Can I change address in the middle of the year?
Yes. Moving needs a new tenancy, a new Ejari and an amendment of the trade licence. We coordinate the three steps so the licence is not left with an old address.
What is the difference between Amer and Tasheel?

Amer centres handle residency and visa transactions for GDRFA. Tasheel centres handle private-sector labour transactions for MOHRE, such as work permits and labour contracts. A new employee usually needs both, in a set order.
What is Tadbeer?
Tadbeer is the network of centres for domestic worker services, such as recruitment, contracts and permits. It is meant for households, not for ordinary company employees.
Can I apply directly online instead of using a centre?

Many services are available through the authorities' online portals and apps, often with UAE Pass login. Centres and service providers help where you want a person to check the file, type the application or handle the follow-up.
What documents do I need for a work permit?
Typically the company's licence and establishment card, the employee's passport and photo, and an offer or contract. Requirements depend on the category, so we confirm the list before filing.
Does a new hire need a labour step or a residency step first?

The labour side, including the offer or contract and work permit, generally comes first, followed by the entry permit or status change, medical fitness, biometrics, visa stamping and Emirates ID. We keep the order on one checklist.
How long does a transaction take?
It depends on the transaction and the authority's review. We give you an estimate once we have the file, and we tell you promptly if a query is raised.
Can a company with a free zone licence use Tasheel?
Free zone companies often follow their free zone authority's labour and residency procedures, and the available channels differ by zone. We confirm the right route for your licence.
What happens if a transaction is rejected?
We read the reason, fix the file and resubmit. Typical causes are a mismatch in names, an expired document, a missing approval or a wrong sequence.
Is there a fee schedule I can see?
Fees are set by each authority and by the service centre. We list each item before you approve the work, and we show the authority's fee separately from our own.
Can you handle many employees at once?
Yes. We create one tracker for the whole group, with each person's status, and we batch submissions where the authority allows it, so you can see progress at a glance.
Who can sponsor a family member in Dubai?

Residents with a valid residence permit may apply to sponsor a spouse and children, and in some cases parents, if they meet the category's conditions on income, accommodation and documents. We check the sponsor's eligibility against the authority's current rules.
What salary do I need to sponsor my family?

Reported figures differ between sources and have changed over time, and some categories have special rules. Check the current GDRFA or ICP requirement before applying; we confirm it for your category and tell you before you pay any fee.
Do marriage and birth certificates need attestation?
Usually yes, for certificates issued abroad. The attestation chain depends on the issuing country, and an Arabic translation is often needed. We plan the route so the slowest step starts first.
Do dependants need health insurance?
Yes, dependants need valid medical insurance as part of the residence file. Our insurance processing service arranges cover that meets the authority's minimum requirements.
Can I sponsor my parents?
In some cases, subject to the authority's rules and the sponsor's status. Extra conditions, such as a deposit or higher income, may apply. We confirm the requirement for your case.
What is a visit visa and how is it different from a residence visa?
A visit visa allows a short stay as a visitor and does not give residency. A residence visa lets a person live in the UAE for a longer period under a sponsor or an employer.
Can you guarantee that the visa will be approved?
No. The authorities decide every application. Our service is preparation and support: a correct and complete file reduces the chance of rejection, but approval is not something we can promise.
How long does the process take?
It depends on the category, the authority's review and how long it takes to attest and translate documents from abroad. We give an estimate after reviewing the file.
My documents are in another language. What do I do?
Documents not in Arabic or English usually need a certified translation, and some need attestation before or after translation. We arrange both and check that names match across all documents.
How do I pay if my family and I are abroad?
Fees are charged in dirhams, which are pegged to the US dollar at 3.6725. You can pay by bank transfer from abroad, and only your own bank's exchange rate and transfer charges apply.
Is health insurance compulsory in Dubai?
Yes. Dubai's health insurance law requires residents to have cover, and employers are responsible for providing it to their employees. Free zone staff are also covered by the requirement.
What is the Essential Benefits Plan?

It is the minimum standard of health cover set under Dubai's insurance framework. Employers may choose a plan that matches or exceeds it. Enhanced plans add benefits such as wider networks, lower co-payments, dental or maternity.
Who pays for an employee's insurance?
The employer is responsible for providing at least the basic plan to employees. Dependants' cover can differ by situation, and sponsors often pay it. We confirm your obligations for your category.
How much does health insurance cost?

The basic plan has been reported at several hundred dirhams per person per year in recent years, and enhanced plans cost more. Premiums depend on age, gender, network and family size, so we ask the insurers for current prices.
What happens if my staff have no valid cover?
Employers can face fines and delays in visa transactions. Reports on the amounts vary, so we confirm the current rule and help you put compliant cover in place quickly.
Can I add family members to a company plan?
Often yes, under the insurer's terms. Dependants can be added at the start or at renewal, and premiums depend on their ages and the plan. We compare group and individual options.
Do I need cover before I apply for a visa?
Valid cover is part of the residence file, so the policy should be ready at the right step. We arrange it so that it matches the visa application and the Emirates ID stage.
Is dental or maternity included?
Not in the basic plan, which has a limited scope. Enhanced plans can include them with waiting periods and limits, so we show the exact terms in the comparison.
Can I keep my existing insurer when I move to Dubai?
Only if the policy is issued by an approved insurer and meets the minimum standard for the UAE. International policies often do not satisfy the residence requirement, so we check this first.
What if I pay from abroad?
Premiums are charged in dirhams, which are pegged to the US dollar at 3.6725. Bank transfers from abroad are accepted by most insurers, and your bank's exchange rate and fees apply.
Which approvals will my business need?

It depends on the activity, the premises and the number of staff. The licence is usually the first approval, and you may also need municipal, health, safety or sector approvals. A short mapping exercise gives you the exact list.
What is a no-objection certificate?

A no-objection certificate, or NOC, is a letter stating that the issuer has no objection to a particular action, such as a transfer or a change of premises. It can come from an employer, landlord, partner or authority.
Can approvals be obtained in parallel?
Often yes. Some approvals depend on others, for example a premises approval needs a confirmed address, but many can run at the same time. We plan them so that dependencies are respected.
How long do approvals take?
It depends on the authority and the activity. The map we prepare includes an expected time per step, and we update you when an authority asks for more information.
Do I need approvals if I only offer consulting services?
Many consultancy activities need no municipal approval, but sector rules still apply to regulated professions. We confirm the position for your activity.
Fire safety is generally reviewed by Civil Defence and building permissions sit with the landlord or the relevant authority. We include them in the project timeline so they are not forgotten.
What if a regulator refuses an approval?
We read the reasons, adjust the application or the plan and resubmit where the rules allow, and we tell you early if a change in activity or premises would be needed.
Can you coordinate with my lawyer or architect?
Yes. We work with lawyers, architects and fit-out contractors so that the documents they produce meet the authorities' requirements and the application is not delayed by format issues.
Are there tax filings connected to a new project?

Yes. A new company or activity can bring corporate tax registration with the Federal Tax Authority, with 9% applying above AED 375,000 of taxable income, and VAT registration above the threshold. Your accountant should confirm your position.
How do I pay if I manage the project from abroad?
Government fees are in dirhams. The dirham is pegged to the US dollar at 3.6725, so dollar transfers are straightforward, and your bank's rate applies for other currencies.
What does a notary public do in Dubai?

A notary verifies the identity of the signers, confirms that they sign knowingly and attests their signatures on the document. The attested document is then accepted by authorities, banks and courts as genuine.
How much does a notary charge?

Under the Dubai fee schedule amended in 2025, AED 300 is charged per signature attested on an instrument or proxy. Private notaries charge under a separate schedule, and drafting, translation and later attestation steps cost extra. We confirm the total before you proceed.
Which documents can be notarised?

Powers of attorney, agreements, declarations, affidavits, share transfers, memorandum amendments and other legal documents. The notary may refuse a document that is unclear or incomplete, so we review it first.
Does the document have to be in Arabic?
Arabic is generally required for UAE use, or an accompanying certified Arabic translation. We prepare the text so that both versions match.
What must I bring to the notary?

Valid passports or Emirates IDs for everyone who signs, with names matching the document, the final text and any company or supporting documents that the document refers to. We give the exact list at booking.
Can I notarise a document if I am not in the UAE?
You can have it notarised in the country where you are and then follow the legalisation and attestation chain for UAE use. We confirm the route for your country before you sign.
Is notarisation enough for use abroad?
Not usually. For use in another country the document normally goes on to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then an embassy attestation or an apostille. We confirm the chain for the destination.
How long does it take?
The notary step is appointment-based and often quick. The onward attestation chain depends on the destination and can take from days to a few weeks.
What if names differ across my documents?
Differences are a frequent cause of rejection. We compare your passport, Emirates ID and the document before the appointment and advise on a declaration or a corrected document if needed.
Can I pay from abroad and in my own currency?
Fees are charged in dirhams, which are pegged to the US dollar at 3.6725. You can pay by bank transfer, and your bank's exchange rate and charges apply for other currencies.
What is the Emirates ID?
It is the identity card issued to UAE residents. It links to the residence visa and is used for banking, insurance, tenancy, driving and many government services.
Is the medical fitness test mandatory?
For most residence categories, yes. It is done at an approved centre, usually with a blood test and chest X-ray, and the result is sent to the authority electronically.
How much does the Emirates ID cost?
Fees depend on the validity period and have changed in recent years, and a centre's service charge is added. We confirm the current total for your case before you pay.
How much does the medical test cost?
Reported figures range from a few hundred dirhams to more, depending on the clinic and whether you choose faster service. We quote the actual price at booking.
In what order do these steps happen?
Typically entry permit or status change first, then medical fitness, biometrics, visa stamping and finally the Emirates ID. Some steps can overlap, and we keep the order on one checklist.
How long does it take to receive the ID?
It depends on the authority and the file. Booking the appointments is quick, and the ID is delivered after processing. We track it and tell you when to expect it.
What if the medical test result is not clear?
The authority informs the applicant and explains the next step, which may be a repeat test or further review. We help you follow the instructions and update the file.
Do children and family members need the same steps?
Dependants generally follow a similar process, with medical fitness, biometrics and an Emirates ID, subject to age rules. See our page on family and visit visa documentation.
Can I renew my Emirates ID with you?
Yes. We prepare renewals, book biometrics where needed and keep the dates in our reminder calendar so that the ID and the visa do not expire at different times.
What about payment from abroad?
Fees are charged in dirhams, pegged to the US dollar at 3.6725. Payments from abroad are accepted by bank transfer, and your bank's exchange rate and charges apply for other currencies.

What the department does

Dubai's Department of Economy and Tourism, known to many business owners by its former name DED, issues and supervises mainland trade licences. Everything that changes the legal identity or permission of a mainland company passes through it: the trade name, the activities, the legal form, the address, the partners and managers, and finally the cancellation. Companies in a free zone are licensed by their own free zone authority and follow that body's rules, not DET's.
Licence types in plain terms
Commercial licences cover trading in goods and certain service activities such as logistics.

Professional licences cover expertise and services, for example consulting, design or engineering. Some professional activities have extra ownership rules, so we check the activity before you plan the shareholding.
Industrial licences cover manufacturing and processing and normally need an industrial premises.

Since the 2021 reforms most mainland activities are open to full foreign ownership, with a limited list of strategic activities still needing a UAE partner or a special approval. Always confirm the current position for your activity. Our company formation service covers the structuring decision in more detail.
Services we file

The process in four steps
1. Requirement check
We compare your activity, ownership and premises with the department's current rules so that the application is built correctly from the start.
2. Documents and approvals

Passports, Emirates IDs where available, the signed memorandum, the registered tenancy and any external approvals are collected. Where another authority must approve the activity first, see our note on Dubai Municipality approvals.
3. Submission
Applications are submitted through the department's online channels. We keep the transaction numbers and answer any request for clarification quickly.
4. Issue and next steps
Once the licence is issued we move on to the immigration card, visas and bank account, where relevant, so the company can start operating without another round of delays.

What a power of attorney does

A power of attorney, or POA, is a signed authority that allows someone else to act in your name. In Dubai it is used to open or run a company file, sign tenancy and bank documents, handle government transactions, sell or buy assets and appear before authorities. The text decides what the agent may do, so a POA written for one purpose and one period is safer than a general authority with no end date.
Types we draft
Special POA for a defined task, such as completing a licence renewal or collecting a certificate
General POA for a wider set of company or personal matters, with clear limits
Company authorisation letter where the company, not an individual, delegates its authority to a PRO (see government transactions liaison)
How the process works
1. Define the authority

We ask what exactly the agent must do, for how long, and with which limits (for example, no authority to sell property or sign loans). We then draft the text in English and Arabic, because UAE authorities generally require Arabic. Our legal typing and form drafting team prepares the final layout.
2. Sign and notarise

In Dubai a notary public attests the signature. The 2025 fee schedule lists AED 300 per signature attested on an instrument or proxy. Larger or complex documents may involve extra work. Our guide to notary public and legal attestations explains the notary step.
3. Signed outside the UAE

A POA signed abroad normally has to be notarised in the country of signing, legalised or apostilled as that country's rules require, and then attested by the UAE embassy in that country and by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in the UAE. The exact chain depends on the country, so we confirm it before you sign anything. For corporate papers, see commercial and corporate document clearing.
4. Delivery and use
You receive the attested original or a certified scan, plus a short note explaining which authorities will accept it and when it expires.

Why the memorandum matters

When partners disagree, when a bank asks who can sign, or when a buyer wants to purchase shares, the Memorandum of Association is the document everyone reads first. A clear MOA lists the shareholders and their percentages, the capital, the manager and signing powers, the licensed activities, the profit and loss sharing, and what happens when a partner wishes to leave. A vague or copied template is a common source of disputes later.

MOA and articles for a new mainland LLC, tailored to the real ownership and management arrangement

The amendment process
1. Agree the change

The partners confirm what is changing. If one partner is selling, the others normally have a right of first refusal under the MOA, so they should sign or waive it in writing. Skipping that step is a typical reason an amendment stops at the notary.
2. Draft in two languages

We prepare the revised text and the Arabic version. Where partners are abroad, they can sign through a notarised power of attorney (POA drafting) or sign in front of a notary in their own country and have the document legalised (document clearing).
3. Notarise

The signatures are attested by a notary public. The Dubai notary schedule lists AED 300 per signature attested on an instrument, and complex documents may have extra costs. Read our guide to notary public and legal attestations for the notary step.
4. File and update the licence

For a mainland company the notarised document is filed with the licensing authority, and the licence is updated to match. Companies in a free zone file with their own authority. Related bank records, visa files and tenancy details should then be updated, and our trade licence amendment service follows through on those.

Why accurate typing still matters

Many UAE processes still depend on a correctly typed application: a labour contract, a licence amendment, a residency form, a tenancy registration or a letter to an authority. A name that differs from the passport by one letter, or a date in the wrong format, is enough for a rejection. Correct typing at the start saves the owner a second trip and a second fee.

What Ejari is

Ejari, meaning "my rent" in Arabic, is the system through which tenancy contracts are registered with the Dubai Land Department. For a business, the Ejari certificate is the proof of the registered business address. Mainland trade licences are normally tied to it, and licence renewals depend on it being current.
Which address options exist?
Mainland: a real, registered lease

A mainland licence generally needs a lease for a premises that fits the activity, registered through Ejari. Industrial activities need suitable facilities, and food and similar activities need premises that can pass municipal checks (Dubai Municipality approvals).
Flexi desk and virtual office

These products give you an address, a desk or a mailing service without a dedicated office. In free zones a flexi desk can satisfy the address requirement for the licence. For mainland licences the position is less clear: advisers report that some professional activities can use a flexi desk where the provider issues an Ejari-compliant lease, while commercial and industrial activities normally need a dedicated unit, and plain virtual office contracts often do not qualify. Because vendors disagree, we check with the licensing authority before you buy.
Free zone office
Free zones usually include an office or desk in the licence package and issue their own lease documents instead of an Ejari.

Which centre does what
Amer centres

Amer centres accept residency and visa transactions on behalf of the General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs in Dubai (GDRFA). Typical tasks include entry permits, status changes, residence visa applications and renewals, and dependents' visas. See visa processing and MOHRE application support and family and visit visa documentation.
Tasheel centres

Tasheel centres are authorised by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MOHRE) to process private-sector labour transactions: work permits, labour contracts, quota and fee payments, complaints and cancellations. They work with the ministry's systems; the residence side of the process is separate and goes through residency channels.
Tadbeer centres
Tadbeer centres serve households that employ domestic workers, covering recruitment, contracts and permits under the domestic worker framework. They are not used for ordinary company staff.

The rule in plain terms

Dubai's health insurance law requires residents to have medical cover, and employers are responsible for providing it to their employees. Dependants such as a spouse and children also need valid cover for their residence files, and in some cases the sponsor pays for it. See the Dubai Health Authority for the framework.

A notary public confirms the identity of the people signing, checks that they understand and sign the document voluntarily, and attests the signature. How many Punjabis live in Dubai?

No official figure for the number of Punjabis in Dubai is published. The Government of India counts Indian nationals in the UAE as a whole and does not publish a breakdown by state of origin. What is on record is the size of the wider Indian community: in August 2023 India's Minister of State for External Affairs told Parliament that about 3.5 million Indians live in the UAE, which makes Indians the largest expatriate community in the country.

For the Sikh community, which is one part of the Punjabi diaspora, published estimates for the whole UAE range from roughly 50,000 to 100,000. These are estimates, not census counts, and Punjabi Hindus, Muslims and Christians are not included in them. Treat any single number you see online for "Punjabis in Dubai" with care unless it names its source and year.
What do Punjabis do in Dubai?

Studies and news reports on migration from Punjab to the Gulf describe many workers in skilled trades and transport. A study of villages in the Doaba region (Kapurthala district) records migrants working mainly as drivers, guards, carpenters and masons after arriving in the Gulf, and The Tribune has reported on masons, welders, plumbers and carpenters from Doaba heading to Gulf countries for work. These sources cover the Gulf in general, not Dubai alone, and they do not give shares by occupation.
Punjabi entrepreneurs have also built businesses in Dubai. One widely reported example is Dr S.P. Singh Oberoi, a Sikh businessman based in Dubai, who has been profiled by Gulf News.
Community life in Dubai

The Guru Nanak Darbar gurdwara in Jebel Ali is the best-known place of worship for Sikhs in Dubai. News reports in 2012 described its opening in Jebel Ali, about 35 km from central Dubai, and noted that before that the community had prayed at a gurdwara in the temple complex in Bur Dubai. The gurdwara serves langar (community meals) and runs weekend classes for children in Punjabi, kirtan and gurdwara etiquette.
Punjab and the Gulf: migration and remittances

Gulf migration from Punjab began in the late 1970s and continues across generations. Money sent home matters to the Indian economy as a whole: according to the Reserve Bank of India's remittance survey, reported by The Tribune, the UAE accounts for about 19% of India's remittance inflows. No state-wise figure for money sent from the UAE to Punjab was found.

This guide walks American owners through the whole route in order: structure, tax checks at home, documents, licence, premises, bank account and visas.
Why American owners look at Dubai

American founders and remote teams use Dubai as a base for clients in the Middle East, South Asia and Africa, and some move operations to work in a time zone that overlaps with Asia and Europe. Because the dirham is pegged to the dollar, contracts and budgets in dollars are easy to plan. Typical clients are consultants, e-commerce and software owners, and small trading firms with clients in the Gulf, South Asia or Africa. Dubai is 12 hours ahead of California in winter and 11 hours ahead in summer, so calls are usually held in the California evening or the Dubai morning.
The route in eight steps
Define the activity, the shareholders and the target customers.
Check the United States side rules with an adviser (tax, reporting, foreign exchange).
Choose mainland or a free zone, then the licence activity.
Reserve the trade name and get initial approval.
Prepare and legalise the documents (see below).
Sign the lease and register it through Ejari (mainland).
Pay fees, receive the licence, register for corporate tax and VAT as needed.
Open the bank account and apply for visas and Emirates ID.
Each step feeds the next, so the order matters. The most common delays come from documents and from the bank, not from the licence itself.
Step 1-3: Structure first, paperwork second

Dubai mainland companies are licensed by the Department of Economy and Tourism, and most activities now allow full foreign ownership. Before you commit, speak to a tax adviser in the United States. US citizens and residents are generally taxed on worldwide income wherever they live, and owners of foreign companies can have reporting duties such as FATCA-related forms, FBAR filings for foreign accounts and information returns for controlled foreign corporations. There is no comprehensive US-UAE income tax treaty, so confirm your position with a US tax adviser before you form the company.
Step 4-5: Names, approvals and documents from the United States

Reserve the trade name, then get initial approval for the activity. Some activities need extra approvals from a regulator. Foreign documents then need to be legalised so that UAE authorities accept them. US documents are normally notarised and then apostilled or authenticated by the state Secretary of State, or by the US Department of State for federal documents, before any further step needed for UAE use. The route depends on the document and on what the UAE side accepts, so we confirm it before you order anything.
Our document clearing and notary public and legal attestation teams plan the chain for you, and our attestation guide explains each stage.
Step 6-7: Premises, licence and taxes

Mainland companies need a registered lease (Ejari) before the licence is issued; a flexible desk may be enough for some activities, see virtual office and Ejari registration. After the licence you register for corporate tax (9% on taxable income above AED 375,000) and for VAT if your turnover requires it. Details are on the Federal Tax Authority website. Renewals matter too; see our licence renewal checklist.
Step 8: Bank account and visas

Banks ask about the owners, the activity and the source of funds. Transfers from US banks to a Dubai company account are usually wires. Banks on both sides ask about the source of funds and the purpose, so keep invoices, agreements and share-capital papers ready. The dirham is pegged to the US dollar at 3.6725, so dollar payments convert at a stable rate. That removes exchange-rate risk on the dirham side for owners who budget and invoice in dollars. Our guide to opening a corporate bank account lists what banks usually ask for.

Residence visas for owners and staff, Emirates ID and medicals follow the licence. We provide document preparation and application support for visas; every visa decision is taken by the UAE authorities, not by us. For long-term residency read our Golden Visa basics.

Treating the Dubai company as a way to escape US reporting. US citizens usually keep filing duties, so the structure should be designed with a US tax adviser from day one.

Frequently asked questions
Can I set up a Dubai company from the United States without travelling?

Often yes for the paperwork: documents can be signed at home and legalised, and a representative can act under a power of attorney, see online power of attorney drafting and attestation. Some steps, like biometrics for the residence visa, need you in the UAE.
Do I need a local partner?
For most mainland activities, no. A limited list of strategic activities needs a UAE partner or special approval, and we check this against your activity.
Is there tax in Dubai?
The UAE has a 9% corporate tax on taxable income above AED 375,000, plus VAT where applicable. Tax in the United States may still apply to you; the IRS (irs.gov) and your own tax adviser can confirm.
How do I move money for the company?
Through your bank, with documents showing the purpose and the source of funds. Check outward-transfer rules in the United States first.
